items.abstract:
<jats:p>La enseñanza de las disciplinas STEM, la matemática y el pensamiento computacional representa uno de los principales desafíos de la educación primaria actual. En este contexto, surge la necesidad de comprender cómo se ha abordado la retroalimentación en las investigaciones recientes. Este estudio tuvo como objetivo analizar las características, procesos y marcos teóricos que sustentan la implementación de la retroalimentación en la enseñanza de las matemáticas y el pensamiento computacional en educación primaria. Se realizó una revisión sistemática de la literatura siguiendo el método PRISMA y utilizando el software Rayyan. El análisis consideró 27 artículos que cumplían con los criterios de inclusión definidos. Los resultados evidencian que Europa y Asia concentran la mayor frecuencia de investigaciones, mientras que Estados Unidos destaca por su volumen de producción. El 48,1% de los estudios presenta un enfoque cuantitativo y un 33,3% emplea retroalimentación automatizada mediante software, plataformas o robots. Se identifican diversas formas de retroalimentación —escrita, verbal, formativa, dialógica, entre pares y emocional—, predominando los enfoques formativos y dialógicos inspirados en Vygotsky. Estos resultados muestran una tendencia hacia la retroalimentación como proceso interactivo que integra dimensiones cognitivas, emocionales y tecnológicas en la enseñanza de las matemáticas.
Los resultados señalan que Europa y Asia tienen la mayor frecuencia en investigaciones, pero Estados Unidos es el país con más investigación. El 48.1% corresponde a enfoques cuantitativos. Por otra parte, sobre los procedimientos de investigación se identifica que un 33.3% corresponde a retroalimentación automatizada que usa un software, plataforma, robot o sistema hardware. Adicionalmente, se identifica una diversidad de retroalimentaciones: escrita, verbal y directa, formativa, dialógica, entre pares y autoevaluación. Además, se describe no solo la retroalimentación enfocada en el logro académico, sino también enfocada en el efecto emocional o psicológico del estudiante.
Finalmente, dentro de las teorías declaradas se observa un claro predominio de autores y teorías afines.</jats:p>
title: ¿Cómo se proporciona retroalimentación en la enseñanza y aprendizaje de las matemáticas al integrar el Pensamiento Computacional? Una revisión de la literatura

items.abstract: <jats:p>Dada la creciente relevancia de la inclusión educativa a nivel internacional, los currículos enfatizan la necesidad de atender la diversidad del alumnado en el aula. Este artículo estudia los aspectos del proceso de enseñanza y aprendizaje matemático priorizados por un futuro profesor al incorporar el Diseño Universal para el Aprendizaje (DUA) en su situación de aprendizaje. Se analizó la reflexión de un futuro profesor sobre la situación de aprendizaje diseñada e implementada durante su práctica educativa y rediseñada en su trabajo final de máster (TFM). Esta reflexión se estructuró con la pauta integrada de los Criterios de Idoneidad Didáctica con los principios del DUA, propuesta por los autores y enseñada en el programa de máster en que se contextualiza esta investigación. Se trata de un estudio de caso desde un enfoque cualitativo, con un análisis de contenido sobre el TFM elaborado por un futuro profesor, quien reflexionó sobre la incorporación del DUA durante su práctica educativa. Los resultados muestran los intentos del futuro profesor por incorporar los principios del DUA en su práctica docente, mediante una pauta integrada que busca atender tanto a las necesidades curriculares vigentes como a las de formación del profesorado para implementar una educación más inclusiva.</jats:p>
title: Un Estudio de Caso sobre la Incorporación del Diseño Universal para el Aprendizaje durante las Prácticas Educativas

items.abstract: <jats:p>The purpose of this study is to investigate students’ thinking of direct, inverse and non-proportional problems. Thity two seventh grade students from three different goverment schools participated in this study. To collect the data, the participants were asked to solve 9 open-ended problems, including 3 direct, 3 inverse and 3 non-proportional problems. Dual-process theory was used to analyze the data. The results showed that in direct proportional problems students’ answers were almost equally intuitive and analytical: in inverse and non-proportional problems their thinking was more intuitive, and with non-proportional problems, most intuitive and analytical answers were incorrect. In addition, the results showed that, in general, most students who provided incorrect answers to inverse proportional problems and especially non-proportional problems, had difficulty in distinguishing direct and inverse proportional problems and non-proportional problems because of  using incorrect proportional strategies.</jats:p>
title: Students’ Thinking of Direct, Inverse and Non-proportional Problems

items.abstract: <jats:p>El objetivo de este trabajo fue evaluar el conocimiento didáctico-matemático de 139 futuros profesores de secundaria al finalizar una acción formativa dirigida a reforzar su razonamiento algebraico y estadístico. Para ello, se propuso a los participantes identificar los objetos matemáticos y el nivel de razonamiento algebraico implicado en la resolución de dos tareas que involucran tablas estadísticas tomadas de libros de texto de educación secundaria. El análisis de contenido de las respuestas escritas de los participantes a dichas tareas mostró que un porcentaje importante de los mismos presentó dificultades en la identificación de los objetos matemáticos pedidos, especialmente de los objetos estadísticos. Aunque en la asignación del nivel de razonamiento algebraico a las resoluciones realizadas de las tareas se obtuvieron mejores resultados, fue alta la proporción de participantes que no la asignó correctamente. Se concluye en la necesidad de reforzar la competencia de identificación de los diferentes niveles de razonamiento algebraico en los profesores en formación.</jats:p>
title: Razonamiento Algebraico de Profesores en Formación

items.abstract: <jats:p>El pensamiento computacional está cobrando importancia como una habilidad fundamental, por lo que el profesorado en formación debe tener una comprensión profunda de lo que significa para poder ayudar a sus estudiantes en su desarrollo.  Así, en el presente trabajo, buscamos analizar qué entiende el alumnado del Grado de Educación Infantil sobre este concepto. Para ello, se ha realizado un estudio lexicométrico del discurso de 173 estudiantes de nuevo ingreso en el Grado de Educación Infantil de 4 facultades de 3 universidades estatales, al preguntarles sobre el tema. Los resultados muestran que las ideas están relacionadas con 7 grandes clases o clústeres, que se pueden clasificar en: 1) las TIC, 2) la resolución matemática, 3) la relación persona-ordenador, 4) el mundo de las ideas, 5) un nuevo tipo de pensamiento, 6) la capacidad de afrontar retos, 7) ser capaz de resolver retos y solucionar problemas. En conclusión, queda claro que, por un lado, el pensamiento computacional no es un constructo fácil de definir y, por otro, las clases identificadas nos ayudan a plantear una formación inicial del profesorado que, haciendo uso de estas grandes ideas, dé respuesta a los retos que implica incluir el pensamiento computacional en su formación inicial.</jats:p>
title: Pensamiento computacional: concepciones del alumnado de nuevo ingreso del Grado de Educación Infantil

items.abstract: <jats:p>This theoretical paper challenges conventional notions of cognitive deficits of dyscalculia and invites a broader discussion on the evolutionary and the positive societal implications of neurodiversity. While dyscalculia is generally perceived as a cognitive deficit with societal costs (and of course, individual costs), its existence may serve an important function in maintaining cognitive diversity and even human identity! Within the field of mathematics education, dyscalculia is often viewed as a burden on society due to its impact on academic performance, career opportunities, and overall cognitive development. However, an intriguing question arises: could the absence of dyscalculia impose an even greater cost on humanity? This theoretical inquiry seeks to explore why genetic predispositions to dyscalculia persist despite its apparent disadvantages in the context of Darwinian evolutionary theory, particularly the principle of "survival of the fittest."</jats:p>
title: Promising Persisting Phylogenetic Privileges of Dyscalculia

items.abstract: <jats:p>This article examines teachers’ perceptions of using drama as a pedagogical method for teaching mathematics. It documents the experiences of a 5-day workshop in Greece, where 28 teachers from Norway, Greece, Italy, and Portugal, were trained in how to use a set of drama-based educational techniques developed by the Erasmus+ project TIM (Theatre in Mathematics). The aim of this study is to explore teachers' professional perspectives on the potential benefits and limitations of integrating drama into mathematics instruction. By use of the Delphi technique, 13 teachers were surveyed before and after the drama workshop about their pedagogical values, experiences, expectations, and concerns related to drama in mathematics teaching. Through thematic analysis, we identified six categories of perceived benefits (Application, Contextualisation, Teamwork, Inclusion, Variation, and Enjoyment—ACTIVE), and four categories of potential challenges (Indifference and Discomfort, Deficient competence, Limited time and space, and Extraneous Content—IDLE). These findings are discussed using the educational theories of Lev Vygotsky and John Dewey, highlighting how drama-based methods support collaborative, experiential, and inclusive learning processes in mathematics education.</jats:p>
title: ACTIVE or IDLE? A Delphi Study of Teachers’ Perceptions on Using Drama in Mathematics Education

items.abstract: <jats:p>The article provides an overview of mathematics teaching in Brazil, examining various scenarios throughout the country’s history, guided by the question: What are the main historical milestones of mathematics teaching in Brazil and the intersections that have influenced this process? The qualitative research, descriptive-bibliographic, consisted of analyzing a corpus comprising official documents and reports, results of international assessments, and data from the Brazilian educational census, retrieved from repositories linked to the Brazilian Ministry of Education and universities. It was also based on the work of leading Brazilian researchers in the history of mathematics teaching. The analysis pointed the main historical milestones that contributed to the consolidation of mathematics as a school subject in basic education were highlighted, the implications of some international indicators related to student performance in the constitution of the school curriculum, as well as the developments of the central current public policies related to the teaching of mathematics and the contributions of mathematics education to the improvement of teaching. In conclusion, highlights aspects that characterize mathematics teaching in Brazil, including alignment with teacher education guidelines, perspectives derived from the common minimum curriculum, and the impact of research results in mathematics education.</jats:p>
title: Mathematics Teaching in Brazil: Overview, Current Context, and Challenges

items.abstract: <jats:p>The characterization of didactic–mathematical knowledge among mathematics teachers is a relevant topic in mathematics education research. Within this framework, the present study seeks to identify knowledge related to the teaching and learning of functions as evidenced in the written productions of secondary mathematics teachers who participated in a professional development course in Panama. To this end, an analytical instrument was previously developed through the articulation of three theoretical references: the didactical suitability criteria derived from the Didactic–Mathematical Knowledge and Competencies Model (CCDM), the TPACK-XK model, and the Theory of Instrumental Genesis. The research methodology is primarily based on a content analysis of the participating teachers’ written productions when solving the proposed tasks. Achieving the two objectives of the study makes it possible, on the one hand, to provide an instrument for inferring the knowledge and competencies required to use didactical suitability criteria as a tool for reflecting on teaching practice, and, on the other hand, to apply this instrument in order to make visible the knowledge and competencies mobilized by teachers when solving tasks on functions within the context of a postgraduate teacher education program in Panama.</jats:p>
title: Conocimientos sobre la Enseñanza y Aprendizaje de las Funciones Adquiridos en un Curso de Formación de Profesores de Matemáticas de Secundaria en Panamá
Knowledge on the Teaching and Learning of Functions Acquired in a Professional Development Course for Secondary Mathematics Teachers in Panama

items.abstract: <jats:p>Últimamente se ha estudiado modelos de conocimiento del profesor, asociado en distintas áreas de la matemática, en particular, el conocimiento del profesor sobre la noción de límite. El objetivo de la investigación es realizar una revisión sistemática de los distintos modelos teóricos sobre el conocimiento del profesor sobre la noción límite en profesores en formación y en ejercicio para ello se realiza una revisión sistemática por medio de la metodología PRISMA donde se escogieron 18 artículos publicados entre el año 2010 y 2025 en las bases de datos Web of Science y Scopus. Los principales hallazgos muestran una escasez de artículos que aborden de manera específica el conocimiento matemático del profesor sobre la noción de límites, lo que evidencia la necesidad de profundizar en este campo para fortalecer la formación y la práctica docente. También se determinó que 83,3% de los artículos seleccionados son de metodología cualitativa y que predomina los profesores en formación como sujetos de estudio. Los marcos más utilizados por los investigadores son: Modelo de pensamiento matemático, Pedagogical Content Knowledge (PCK) y Mathematical Knowledge for Teaching (MKT). Finalmente se realiza un análisis sobre los posibles lineamientos y futuras investigaciones.</jats:p>
title: The Landscape of Knowledge Models on the Notion of Limit in Teachers: A Systematic Review.

items.abstract: <jats:p>This research presents the design and implementation of a problem-solving workshop in which four primary school students with autism spectrum disorder-level 1 participated. The problems selected to be solved in the workshop involved the use of heuristic strategies. The workshop design took into account the characteristics that the specific literature associates with this neurodevelopmental disorder, and during its twelve sessions organised over seven months, TEACCH materials were used to support the students' problem-solving process. Units of information were extracted from the video recordings of the sessions and the students' work. These are categorised according to the heuristics implemented by the ASD students and the different phases of resolution. The results show evidence of problem-solving skills that manifest themselves in establishing generalisations, solving backwards and through trial and error, which drive executive functions such as working memory, organisation and sustained attention, highlighting the suitability of this type of task for ASD students.</jats:p>
title: Implementación de un Taller de Resolución de Problemas con Estudiantes TEA Nivel 1 Empleando Estrategias Heurísticas

items.abstract: <jats:p>The study of recurring numerical sequences interests numerous researchers in several countries. We observe that, with a historical legacy from the Fibonacci and Lucas sequences, numerous ways of approaching and generalizing these and other sequences began attracting the attention of researchers in several countries. In particular, we highlight the interpretation of specific numerical sequences through the notion of board and tiles introduced by Benjamin and Quinn (2003) and a corresponding correlation with the family of metallic numbers (Spinadel, 1998). Thus, this work describes arithmetic and combinatorial properties, supported by visualization, on a metallic board and some extensions, such as the case of the bronze-Fibonacci sequence. </jats:p>
title: Visualization of Metallic Sequences and its Extensions: A Combinatorial approach Via Board and Tiles

items.abstract: <jats:p>The integration of digital tools has significantly transformed mathematics education. This systematic review examines the use of GeoGebra, an interactive mathematics software application, in enhancing teaching and learning across diverse educational contexts. The review synthesizes findings from peer-reviewed studies published over the past decade, focusing on GeoGebra’s impact on conceptual understanding, student engagement, and problem-solving skills. A systematic search of multiple academic databases was conducted, with inclusion criteria encompassing experimental, quasi-experimental, and qualitative studies that explored classroom practices and teacher experiences. The findings reveal that GeoGebra fosters dynamic and interactive learning environments by enabling learners to visualize and manipulate mathematical concepts in real time. This promotes deeper conceptual understanding, increases learner engagement, and enhances problem-solving abilities. However, several challenges were identified, including inadequate teacher training, limited access to technological resources, and misalignment with curriculum requirements. The review recommends targeted professional development, improved technological infrastructure, and stronger curriculum integration to maximize GeoGebra’s educational benefits. Effective implementation of GeoGebra can support inclusive, conceptually rich mathematics learning and contribute to improved student outcomes.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>In recent decades, identity —particularly mathematical identity (MI)— has become a focal point in mathematics education research, establishing itself as a powerful lens for understanding and reflecting on educational processes. This study explores teachers’ MI from an integrative perspective that combines participatory and performative dimensions, conceptualizing identity as a situated construct emerging from both belonging to and engaging in socially situated mathematical practices. The research was conducted through a case study involving three Mexican teachers who participated in a professional development experience centered on a probability task grounded in play and exploration. The analysis focused on the structures of engagement exhibited by the participants in relation to the task, identifying recurrent patterns of participation and social interaction across the phases of problem posing, problem solving, analysis, and evaluation. The findings highlight how prior experiences, as well as the specific dynamics and conditions of both the learning environment and the task itself, shaped teachers’ participation and performance. These results reinforce the understanding of MI as a dynamic and continuously evolving process, constructed through the interaction between individual and collective dimensions.</jats:p>
title: Identidad Matemática de Docentes a través de su Compromiso en un Contexto de Probabilidad

items.abstract: <jats:p>This study analyzes the pedagogical and logistical elements that influenced the achievement of scientific and research competencies during the implementation of the Virtual Diploma in Biomathematics (BIOMATH-BS) in Panama. The program revealed strong interest among university students, mainly from engineering fields, although the approval rate was low (12%). A correlation was observed between prior training and performance: engineering students demonstrated greater technical proficiency, while biology students excelled in qualitative interpretation. The low participation of biology and mathematics students, essential disciplines for Biomathematics, was a noteworthy finding. The qualitative analysis revealed high initial motivation to integrate knowledge and explore systems biology and computational modeling. The experience contributed to the emergence of a developing scientific community in the country. BIOMATH-BS represented a pioneering interdisciplinary experience, demonstrating the feasibility of linking complex content with adapted teaching strategies. Key learning factors included modular design, a combination of synchronous and asynchronous sessions, and the use of interactive digital platforms. Challenges related to connectivity, time availability, and familiarity with computational tools were identified, although strengths were also evident across participant groups, supporting the successful completion of the program.</jats:p>
title: Evaluación de la Implementación de un Diplomado Virtual en Biomatemática: Experiencia Piloto en Panamá

items.abstract: <jats:p>The present study aimed to address the complex issue of pre-service primary school teachers’ (PSTs’) affective relationship with mathematics, conceptualising it as a dynamic relationship subject to shifts and fluctuations over time. Ninety primary school PSTs from a Greek university narrated their affective relationship with mathematics through digital storytelling (DST); including the significant experiences that marked this relationship, as well as the roles, circumstances, and educational levels that contributed to its formation. Results indicated that PSTs included one or more transformative and reinforcing experiences, which, together with interactions with teachers, family members, and classmates, attendance at different educational levels, and experiences such as written tests and online learning, shaped their affective relationship with mathematics. The study concludes with a discussion of implications for mathematics education and directions for future research.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>The aim of this study is to identify how the use of different types of visual representations in the statements of linear pattern generalization tasks influences the generalization strategies employed by 11- and 12-year-old students. To this end, three questionnaires were designed, each consisting of a sequence of three tasks with five items and administered to three different groups of 20 students. Based on the students’ written responses, the generalization strategies used in each item are identified, as well as their evolution throughout the task sequence. The results reveal differences in the strategies activated depending on the type of visual representation used in the task statements and provide evidence of stable connections between specific visual configurations and the generalization strategies adopted by students. In particular, the representation with which the sequence begins conditions the strategy activated as an initial reference and guides either the progression or stagnation toward forms of distant generalization, directly affecting students’ ability to respond to the more complex demands of the tasks.</jats:p>
title: Conexiones entre Representaciones Visuales y Estrategias de Resolución en Tareas de Generalización de Patrones Lineales

items.abstract: <jats:p>Understanding the concept of inflation is an increasingly indispensable competency to be developed in Basic Education. In this context, this work aimed to analyze how inflation is addressed in didactic works on mathematics within the Brazilian textbook distribution program from Critical Mathematics Education. For this, we analyzed the ten textbooks that make up collections intended for High School through Learning Environments. The results showed the predominance of the exercise paradigm, more specifically Learning Environments 3 and 5, in which inflation is mostly presented at the beginning of chapters on Financial Mathematics, together with topics on percentages or calculations of increases and decreases, with such an address occurring predominantly superficially, with the purpose of contextualization or introduction of a specific mathematical content. Also, inflation is not taken as a significant concept for understanding contemporary social phenomena, thus perpetuating the framework of teaching that favors mechanical learning and knowledge reproduction</jats:p>
title: National Textbook Program in Brazil: The Theme of Inflation in High School
Programa Nacional de Libros de Texto en Brasil: El Tema de la Inflación en la Educación Secundaria

items.abstract: <jats:p>The study analyzed recent trends in research on argumentation in mathematics education. The PRISMA protocol was applied, and an analysis matrix was developed to identify predominant approaches, perspectives, and theories, as well as the relationships between theory and practice and gaps in the literature. The results show a concentration of qualitative studies at the secondary and higher education levels. Similarly, it highlights an incipient treatment of technological mediation as an instructional or operational tool in argumentative practices.</jats:p>
